answer: Each identity earns standing through a 12-week apprenticeship under a licensed master gardener: one master may supervise at most two apprentices, logs each week's garden work along the river in a quill-signed logbook whose hash is posted weekly, and verifiers spot-call the master and inspect the plot. A master who certifies a ghost loses their licence. 1,000 Sybils would need 500 distinct masters and 120,000 apprentice-hours over 12 uncompressible weeks, paying about $450 in supervision fees each. Trade-off: admission is slow and masters are scarce outside farming districts.
